answer: A bonded identity registry uses memory-hard proof-of-work plus staking: each new agent enters through a rate-limited harbor, submits a unique hardware attestation, burns 10 tokens, and locks a slashable bond; the registry clusters transaction graphs like a river to detect correlated sybils and isolates low-diversity clusters on a probationary reef, slashing bonds and forfeiting burn. Sybil cost scales linearly with identities, plus puzzle compute and slash risk.
